hypothesis: Remaining live decode buffers hold partly free CUDA allocator segments. Public memory snapshots will separate inactive bytes in live segments from fully inactive segments. One candidate uses Torch2.5.1 documented experimental expandable_segments:True to reduce layout waste.
control: Exact native-reuse policy and charged prefill cleanup in every arm; source/prompt/model/teacher/capacities fixed. Two identical measurements per fresh process; compare separate default-layout and expandable-layout processes.
primary: At least10% lower decode GPU reserved peak beyond charged cleanup control. Active/model-wide peak and complete512MiB ceiling reported separately.
progression: First four fresh process pilots, public snapshots and numerical preservation. A short hash-instrumented pair does not prove latency. If memory primary passes, run fresh-process 50-step blocks with warmup and alternating process order; then mandatory preservation/lifetime stress. No global environment, CLI/default or dependency change.
